notes:
Here are verse-by-verse notes on Galatians 5. I ran out of searches before covering everything, so some verses have only thin notes. Those gaps are listed at the end.

---

**v. 1**
- **Traditional reading.** Guzik says Christ is the one who made us free; we can't free ourselves. Freedom is a gift received by faith, and struggling to free ourselves only tangles us further. If we live in bondage to a legal relationship with God, it isn't because God wills it. He says "stand fast" means it takes effort to stay free, because someone freed in Jesus can be deceived into placing themselves back into slavery. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/galatians-5/
- Guzik links the "yoke" to Peter's words in Acts 15:10. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/galatians-5/
- Matthew Henry says Christ freed us in two ways. His merits met the demands of the broken law, and his authority released us from the Jewish ceremonial rules. Our duty is to hold to that freedom and not go back to the law of Moses.  https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Gal/Gal_005.cfm
- Wesley takes the liberty to mean freedom "From the ceremonial law." https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/galatians/5.htm

**v. 2**
- Guzik says Paul isn't against circumcision as such. For Gentile Galatians, though, being circumcised meant coming under the law and trusting themselves instead of Jesus as their righteousness. He quotes Calvin: "Whoever wants to have a half-Christ loses the whole." https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/galatians-5/
- Henry draws the lesson that though Jesus Christ is able to save to the uttermost, yet there are multitudes whom he will profit nothing. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Gal/Gal_005.cfm

**v. 3**
- Guzik says anyone who comes to God on the basis of keeping the law must keep all of it, perfectly. He quotes Lightfoot: circumcision is the seal of the law, so someone who accepts it signs up to fulfil the law and can't fall back on Christ's grace. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/galatians-5/
- Jamieson-Fausset-Brown (JFB) adds that Christ himself was circumcised and so took on keeping the whole law for us. Anyone who tries to keep it for himself as a way to be justified cuts himself off from that grace.  https://biblehub.com/commentaries/galatians/5-4.htm

**v. 4** (Protestant traditions really differ here)
- **Shared reading.** Ellicott says "are justified" strictly means "*seek* to be justified." In his view grace is not here a state or disposition in the believer, but a divine act or relation. https://biblehub.com/galatians/5-4.htm
- **Can a true believer lose salvation?** One Bible Hub article sets out three positions:
  - Some Arminian writers: a believer can lose salvation.
  - The traditional Reformed view: real believers who flirt with the law lose joy, assurance and liberty, but not eternal life.
  - A "mixed audience" view: people relying on the law were never born again in the first place.

  The article prefers the third.  https://biblehub.com/q/Meaning_of_fallen_from_grace_in_Gal_5_4_2.htm
- **Eternal-security readings.**
  - Matthew Poole says "grace" here isn't a state of grace (from which none can fall totally and finally), but the grace of the gospel. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/galatians/5-4.htm
  - Barnes says Paul is only stating a hypothesis. On his reading the verse can't prove a true Christian has fallen away, unless it also proves people can be justified by the law. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/galatians/5-4.htm
  - Gill suggests the people meant may have been Christians in name only. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/galatians/5-4.htm
  - GotQuestions says the verse doesn't mention salvation or the believer's security. It reads the Greek as meaning "estranged" or "separated from." https://www.gotquestions.org/fall-from-grace.html
- **A reading closer to the other side.** Meyer describes the Galatians' relationship of grace with God as something capable of being lost. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/galatians/5-4.htm
- **Guzik's middle position.** He says falling from grace is a real danger but often misunderstood. It isn't about immoral behaviour. Someone can fall from grace without gross sin, simply by no longer relying on God's grace through faith. He quotes Boice: to fall from grace is to fall into legalism. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/galatians-5/
- **Early church writers** (as reported by Bible Hub): Chrysostom said falling from grace means losing all the benefits of Christ's death. Augustine distinguished professing grace from actually having it.  https://biblehub.com/q/Meaning_of_fallen_from_grace_in_Gal_5_4_2.htm
- I couldn't find a Wesleyan or Methodist writer's own comment on this verse.

**v. 5**
- Guzik says people walking by the Spirit wait for righteousness instead of trying to earn it: No one is a legalist through the Spirit. He quotes Wuest, who reads the "hope of righteousness" as the practical righteousness the Spirit produces in daily life. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/galatians-5/
- Others read it as the future reward:
  - Wesley: The righteousness we hope for, and full reward of it. This righteousness we receive of God through faith; and by faith we shall obtain the reward. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/galatians/5.htm
  - Matthew Henry's Concise: believers wait for eternal life as God's gift, not because of their own works. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/galatians/5-4.htm

**v. 6** (a key verse in Catholic–Protestant debate)
- **Protestant readings.**
  - Ellicott: faith is the driving force and love is the rule that guides it. Faith makes a man seek to do the will of Christ; love tells him what that will is. https://biblehub.com/galatians/5-6.htm
  - Pulpit Commentary: love isn't something added to faith from outside but a product of faith itself. https://biblehub.com/galatians/5-6.htm
  - One commentary on Bible Hub calls "working through love" Paul's answer in advance to the charge that "faith only" leads to lawless living. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/galatians/5-6.htm
  - Guzik: if your faith doesn't work through love, it isn't real faith. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/galatians-5/
  - Henry: true faith is a working grace: it works by love. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Gal/Gal_005.cfm
- **Catholic reading.**
  - A Catholic Answers article teaches that a person reaches heaven through faith that is always "working through love." https://www.catholic.com/magazine/online-edition/galatians-216-and-sola-fide
  - Another Catholic Answers piece quotes Pope Benedict XVI: Luther's "faith alone" is true if it is not opposed to faith in charity, in love. It also notes that the Reformers themselves spoke of faith showing itself through love. https://www.catholic.com/audio/tjap/faith-alone-what-everybody-gets-wrong
  - The Catholic Douay-Rheims Bible translates the phrase as "faith that worketh by Charity." https://biblehub.com/catholic/galatians/5-6.htm

**v. 7**
- Guzik quotes Lightfoot: "hindered" is a military image for breaking up a road so no one can use it. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/galatians-5/
- Henry pictures the Christian life as a race. It isn't enough just to run; you have to run well. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Gal/Gal_005.cfm

**v. 8**
- Henry says the "persuasion" was the claim that the Galatians must be circumcised and keep the law of Moses. Since it didn't come from God, he implies it came from Satan and his agents. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Gal/Gal_005.cfm

**v. 9**
- Guzik says yeast almost always stands for evil influence in Jewish thinking. Even a small dose of legalism can spoil everything. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/galatians-5/
- Henry draws the lesson that churches are in danger if they tolerate people spreading destructive errors. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Gal/Gal_005.cfm

**v. 10**
- Guzik says Paul's confidence was really in the Lord, who is able to keep the Galatians. He also says judgment is sure for the troublemaker no matter how respected he is. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/galatians-5/
- Henry says Paul blames the false teachers more than the Galatians, and that we should hope the best even of people we fear the worst about. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Gal/Gal_005.cfm

**v. 11**
- Guzik says Paul's being persecuted proves he no longer preached circumcision. He explains Timothy's circumcision as being for evangelism among Jews, not for salvation. He argues legalism takes away the "offense of the cross," which he calls really the cross's glory. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/galatians-5/
- Henry says Paul could have avoided persecution by preaching circumcision. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Gal/Gal_005.cfm

**v. 12** (two ways of reading it)
- **Castration.** Guzik takes it as Paul wishing the agitators would go all the way and castrate themselves. He links it to the ritual castration practised by pagan priests in Galatia, and quotes Rendall connecting the word to the worship of the goddess Cybele. He also sees an echo of Deuteronomy 23:1, which barred such men from the assembly. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/galatians-5/
- **Church discipline.** Henry reads it differently: not cut off from Christ and all hopes of salvation by him, but cut off by the censures of the church. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Gal/Gal_005.cfm

**v. 13**
- Guzik says true freedom is freedom from having to earn righteousness, not "doing whatever we want." He quotes Rendall: the word "opportunity" was a military term for a base of operations. Serving one another in love is the antidote, following Jesus' own example. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/galatians-5/

**v. 14**
- JFB says "faith-only" teaching doesn't throw out the heart of the law, because the whole law is fulfilled in love, and love is how faith works. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/galatians/5-6.htm

**v. 15**
- JFB notes that love is the complete opposite of the quarrelling going on among the Galatians. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/galatians/5-6.htm

**v. 16**
- Guzik says the legalist's fear that liberty leads to sin is simply wrong. He quotes Wuest: the Spirit's inner restraint works better than outside laws, much as a policeman on the corner deters crime better than posted rules. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/galatians-5/
- John Piper (Desiring God) says walking by the Spirit stops bad desires before they mature: you nip the desires of the flesh in the bud. https://www.desiringgod.org/messages/the-war-within-flesh-versus-spirit

**v. 17** (traditions differ on how this relates to Romans 7)
- **Struggle inside the believer.**
  - The Geneva Study Bible (Reformed) says the flesh dwells even in the regenerated man, but the Spirit reigns, even though not without great strife, and points to Romans 7. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/galatians/5-17.htm
  - GotQuestions sees an inner struggle in every believer that lasts until Christ returns. https://www.gotquestions.org/Spirit-against-the-flesh.html
- **Not the same as Romans 7.**
  - Meyer says in Romans 7 the flesh fights the person's own better will and wins. In believers the flesh fights the Holy Spirit, and the person can obey the Spirit. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/galatians/5-17.htm
  - Constable also holds that the conflict here isn't the one in Romans 7. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/galatians/5-17.html
- **Wesley's hopeful reading.** He takes the clause as stating a purpose: That, being thus strengthened by the Spirit, ye may not fulfil the desire of the flesh, as otherwise ye would do. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/wen/galatians-5.html
- **Barnes.** He says "cannot do" is much stronger than the Greek. The verse could just as well mean the Spirit holds the Christian back from evil they would otherwise do. https://www.studylight.org/bible/eng/bsb/galatians/5-17.html
- **Piper.** Read together, verses 16–17 are mainly about the Spirit's victory, not the war. https://www.desiringgod.org/messages/the-war-within-flesh-versus-spirit
- **Ellicott.** Paul's contrast between flesh and Spirit isn't dualism; he doesn't treat the body as evil in itself. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/galatians/5-17.htm

**v. 18**
- Wesley: led by the Spirit - Of liberty and love, into all holiness. Ye are not under the law - Not under the curse or bondage of it; not under the guilt or the power of sin. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/galatians/5.htm

**vv. 19–21**
- Guzik groups the list into sexual, religious, interpersonal and social sins. He says people who habitually practise them show they never received God's Spirit. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/galatians-5/
- Wesley:
  - "Works" is plural because these sins are separate and often clash with each other, while the "fruit" of the Spirit (v. 22) is singular because it all hangs together. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/galatians/5.htm
  - By "flesh" Paul means the corruption of human nature, as it spreads through all the powers of the soul, not just the body. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/galatians/5.htm
  - Paul listed the sins the Galatians were most inclined to. https://www.ccel.org/ccel/wesley/notes.i.x.vi.html
- On v. 21, Guzik says Paul's firmness fits the Bible's idea of conversion. He also notes Paul's "as I did before" shows that teaching on how to live was a regular part of his message. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/galatians-5/

**vv. 22–23**
- Guzik:
  - The fruit is singular, a cluster that should show in every believer, with love first because it includes the rest. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/galatians-5/
  - "Gentleness" means being teachable, not timid. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/galatians-5/
  - The Spirit's self-control works for the good of others, not just oneself. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/galatians-5/
- Wesley calls love The root of all the rest. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/wen/galatians-5.html
- Cornelius à Lapide (1614) says Paul's list isn't complete, and that charity is the parent of all the rest. https://www.studylight.org/bible/eng/kjv/galatians/5-13.html
- Calvin's commentary carries a note quoting Bishop Sanderson on why it's called "fruit" and not "work." https://ccel.org/ccel/calvin/calcom41/calcom41.iii.vii.v.html
- Precept Austin:
  - The fruit is evidence of real faith, not an option. https://www.preceptaustin.org/galatians_522
  - Spiritual gifts differ from believer to believer, but the fruit shows in every believer. Gifts can be imitated; character can't. https://www.preceptaustin.org/galatians_522
  - One writer quoted there: you can't hang the fruit on a life from outside like ornaments on a Christmas tree. https://www.preceptaustin.org/galatians_522

**v. 24**
- Piper names the puzzle: verse 17 describes a live war in the Christian, yet verse 24 says the flesh is crucified. https://www.desiringgod.org/messages/the-war-within-flesh-versus-spirit
- Henry says believers haven't yet fully won. The flesh still troubles them, but it no longer rules, and they are working to destroy it completely. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/galatians/5-17.html
- Guzik applies the verse to dying to besetting sins every day in the power of Christ's resurrection. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/joshua-7/

**v. 25**
- Henry: if we say we've received the Spirit, we should show it by the Spirit's fruit in our lives. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/galatians/5-22.html

**v. 26**
- Wesley says people who don't follow the Spirit closely slide easily into wanting praise. The result is provoking to envy them that are beneath us, and envying them that are above us. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/wen/galatians-5.html

---

**Gaps**
- **Enduring Word:** the page cut off after the verse 13 heading, so Guzik's notes on vv. 14–26 come only from search excerpts.
- **Traditions not covered:** I found nothing from Lutheran sites (lcms.org, 1517.org), Pentecostal sites, Anglican sources, or Wesleyan comment on v. 4.
- **Other views:** I found no NET Bible notes, Bible Odyssey articles, Orthodox sources (oca.org), or material on prosperity, word-of-faith or hyper-grace teaching. Those sections are left out.
- **Thin verses:** vv. 14, 15 and 25 have only one source each.
